title: Hover in the dap-view window evaluates the word under the cursor, not the tree node
description: With the cursor inside the Scopes tree, <leader>de evaluates vim.fn.expand('<cexpr>') against the rendered text of the tree line. On a Go session that text is a rendered value, so on the line 'Inner = main.Level2 {Inner: ma...' the cursor lands on the type name and delve answers 'Unable to evaluate expression: package main has no function Level2'. The error float then draws over the tree, which is how the user hit it. Same class of failure on Python, where the word under the cursor is a repr fragment rather than an expression.
design: actions.hover() falls back to util/exprs.get_current_expr(), which is expand('<cexpr>') in normal mode. The tree already carries what is needed: state.line_to_variable_path maps a line to a node path and state.variable_path_to_evaluate_name maps that path to the adapter's evaluateName. Branch on the current window being state.winnr (and on the current section being scopes or watches) and use that pair; fall back to the current behaviour only in a code window. The hover tree itself has the same pair under hover_path_to_*. Parent issue for the user-visible report in dv-kyf.
acceptance_criteria: Invoking hover while the dap-view window is the current window resolves the expression from the tree node under the cursor (its evaluateName), not from the buffer text. The type name of a rendered value is never sent to the adapter. Headless case under both hosts, and on a value whose rendering contains an identifier that is not a valid expression.
close_reason: Resolved tree hover expressions from the node evaluateName; added tab/split regression coverage

title: No exception support: cannot arm exception breakpoints or read exception details
description: Two related holes. There is no tool wrapping setExceptionBreakpoints, so an agent cannot ask the debuggee to stop when an exception is raised or uncaught; it can only guess a line. And when the program does stop on an exception, session_status reports the stop reason and description but never issues the DAP exceptionInfo request, so the exception type, message and stack detail are unavailable.
design: capabilities.exceptionBreakpointFilters is already on the session object. Add lua/dap-mcp/tools/exceptions.lua with list_exception_filters and set_exception_breakpoints. In status.compose, when last.reason == 'exception', pcall a util.request for 'exceptionInfo' with the stopped thread id and attach it; keep it best-effort like the rest of the composer so a failure never breaks status.
acceptance_criteria: A tool lists the adapter's exception breakpoint filters (from capabilities.exceptionBreakpointFilters) and sets which are active. When the debuggee stops with reason 'exception', session_status includes the exceptionInfo payload: exception id, description, break mode and details. Verified against debugpy, which reports raised and uncaught filters.

title: Capture program output: agents cannot see what the debuggee printed
description: Nothing in the MCP listens to the DAP 'output' event. status.lua subscribes to event_stopped, event_terminated, event_exited and event_initialized only. An agent therefore has no way to read the debuggee's stdout, stderr, the adapter's console output, or REPL output, which is how most real debugging actually proceeds. It bites hardest on Go: with delve's outputMode=remote the program's stdout goes to the dap-repl, so there is not even a terminal buffer to fall back on.
design: Subscribe to dap.listeners.after.event_output in status.lua's install(), appending {category, output, timestamp} to a bounded ring buffer (size from config.response, default a few hundred entries), cleared on event_initialized. Add lua/dap-mcp/tools/output.lua exposing get_output with optional category filter and paging that mirrors vars.page. Consider surfacing the tail in session_status so the common case needs no second call.
acceptance_criteria: A get_output tool returns recent program output with its DAP category (stdout, stderr, console, telemetry), newest-last, paged and clamped like every other response. Output is captured from session start, not from the first call. session_status reports how many lines are buffered so an agent knows to look. Covered in tests/run.lua for both a stdout-producing and a stderr-producing fixture.

title: Richer MCP tooling
description: The agent-facing MCP surface (nvim-dap-mcp/) covers the debug lifecycle well for discovery, launch, breakpoints, execution, stack and variables, but an audit against the lifecycle on 2026-09-15 found four gaps that cost an agent real debugging ability, plus some smaller ones and a placement problem. This epic collects them; children are independent and can be picked up in any order.
design: Current surface, 22 tools: list_configurations, start_session, stop_session, session_status, wait_for_pause | list_breakpoints, set_breakpoint, remove_breakpoint | control (step_over/into/out, resume, pause, run_to_line) | list_threads, get_stack, select_frame | get_variables, get_value, set_variable, evaluate | ui_open, ui_close, ui_undock, ui_dock, ui_host | neovim_ping. session_status is the fat one-call snapshot: state, stop reason, current frame, source context, top 10 frames and the first scope's variables, values clamped at 200 cells with full_value_ref for the rest.

title: No get_scopes tool: agents can only see the first scope of a frame
description: The MCP surface has no tool that lists a frame's scopes. The only place scopes are requested is the session_status composer, which takes scopes[1] and discards the rest. On debugpy that means an agent sees Locals and can never reach Globals; on any adapter it cannot reach Registers or class-variable scopes. get_variables needs a variables_reference, and nothing hands out the reference for a non-first scope.
design: Add lua/dap-mcp/tools/scopes.lua registering get_scopes, taking an optional frame_id and defaulting to session.current_frame like the other tools do. Request 'scopes' via util.request and render each entry. Consider whether session_status should also list the scope names it did not inline, so an agent knows more exists without a second call.
acceptance_criteria: A get_scopes tool returns every scope of a frame with its name, variables_reference, expensive flag and named/indexed counts, defaulting to the selected frame. An agent can reach Globals on debugpy through it. Covered in tests/run.lua.

title: Hover on a large value (matrix) stalls and never shows a float
description: Hovering the 30x30 'matrix' variable takes a very long time and no float appears; the editor feels hung. Reproduced by the user on Go (dap-playground/go/main.go) and present in the Python fixture too, which has the same 30x30 matrix. Other variables on the same frame hover instantly, so it scales with the size of the value rather than being a fixed failure.
design: Suspects, in order. (1) hover/view.show measures width over the whole rendered value; a 30x30 matrix is thousands of cells and the float width computation plus nvim_win_set_width run per render. tree.max_value_width clamping (config default 60) may not be applied on the hover path at all, only in the scopes tree. (2) Expanding a 900-element array issues a variables request per level and renders every child. (3) The evaluate itself may be slow in delve for a large aggregate; if so, show the float first and fill it when the response lands rather than blocking. Measure before fixing: time the evaluate request separately from the render.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering any variable in the fixtures, matrix included, shows a float within a fraction of a second. Large values are clamped for display the way the tree already clamps them. The editor is never blocked while the adapter call is in flight. A headless timing assertion on the matrix value.

title: Scopes tree: expansion leaves stale/closed folds in the dap-view window

Also suspect foldlevel: freshly rendered deeper lines inherit a level above foldlevel and come back closed after a re-render. Check views/options.lua, tree/fold.lua, and whether the render path resets folds (a synchronous parse + zv/zR equivalent) after rewriting buffer lines.

title: Bound evaluation waits for adapters that do not answer watch-context requests
description:

Its evaluate handler supports repl and hover contexts but only logs unsupported contexts; it sends no DAP response for context=watch. The binary demo initially stalled inside a trusted Lua decoder callback calling session:request(evaluate, context=watch). Native watch evaluation also requests watch context. The same read-only expression succeeds in repl context. Current demo explicitly uses repl for Lua, which is a local compatibility workaround.

Evidence/source: deps/osv/lua/osv/init.lua handlers.evaluate, branches around lines 355/479 and unsupported-context logging around 602; permanent demo scripts are under ~/scratch/nvim-dap-view-demo.

Follow-up: reproduce unanswered evaluate requests with a fake adapter and verify bounded failure/cleanup for watch evaluation and documented decoder helpers. The upstream adapter should return an unsuccessful response instead of dropping requests.

title: Surface invalid binary DAP value types instead of leaving the variables view blank
description:
Reproduced with one-small-step-for-vimkind at 1af6ffb9b5229a856e8090fa2f690e0931a5aace during the real Lua protobuf/gzip demo. Raw Lua strings containing NUL and non-UTF8 bytes arrive in DAP variable.value/evaluate.result as arrays of byte numbers rather than the strings required by DAP. Evaluating string.char(0,255) in REPL context confirms result_type=table and length=2. Putting raw binary strings directly in locals left the scopes buffer blank; byte arrays cannot be used where decoder preparation/rendering expects a string. This is an upstream adapter formatting problem with a client robustness consequence.

Reproducer: ~/scratch/nvim-dap-view-demo/binary.lua without the buffer wrapper, attached using binary-init.lua and the locally cloned OSV adapter. The current demo uses a wrapper and reads actual data through base64 slices; it does not patch the adapter or prove raw-string rendering works.

Follow-up: validate malformed variable/evaluation values at the integration boundary and report an actionable rendering error rather than silently abandoning the render; isolate a bad node where possible. Capture a small adapter replay and identify an upstream adapter fix that escapes display values without altering underlying data.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed DAP value/result types produce a visible diagnostic without hanging or blanking valid siblings. A regression covers binary strings containing NUL/0xff. Document or link the upstream OSV cause; do not silently coerce arbitrary arrays into claimed-complete bytes.

title: Make MCP paused reads coherent through the existing pause module
description:
Backlog recommendation only. User explicitly requested no implementation during stabilization.

Source: independent Sol priority review of eef1446 plus parent fixes; source drift to5df148d recorded. Parent re-read the final wait readiness guard; these remain design recommendations, not reproduced release blockers. Statechart evidence: docs/audits/statechart/2026-11-07/README.md.

**Description / confirmed evidence.** Pause ownership rules are split between `nvim-dap-mcp/lua/dap-mcp/pause.lua:11–19,29–57,64–78`, `tools/wait.lua:96–128` (stack readiness and post-compose checks), and `tools/stack.lua:28–44,85–104` (session/thread/token fencing and frame lookup). Meanwhile `status.lua:121–140,148–171,177–208` yields through stack/scopes/variables and itself has no final ownership check; the wait tool supplies one externally. `status.lua:13–49` also stores stop metadata globally, independent of the session argument of its listeners. This proves scattered policy, not a newly replayed mixed-snapshot or multi-session bug.

**Proposed seam / deletion.** Deepen the already useful pause module with `capture(session)`, `is_current(snapshot)`, `ready_frame(snapshot)` and pause-owned frame lookup/retention, rather than adding a generic async module. Have a single status read operation return a coherent result or an explicit stale outcome. Put readiness knowledge (old frame/stack identity) there. Keep serialization/optional locals in status; keep waiting/listener/timer settlement in wait. Delete equivalent session/thread/token checks and the wait tool's knowledge of `previous_frame`/`previous_frames` after callers migrate. Scope last-stop metadata by session if multi-session characterization confirms that requirement.

**Dependencies / sequence.** None beyond stabilization. First characterize already-stopped, stop-in-progress and frame-advertisement behavior through existing callers; then deepen pause; migrate stack callers; finally status and wait. Do not require UI or decoders to load MCP.

**Acceptance / validation.** Real nvim-dap event_stopped can yield while loading threads/stackTrace; stopped_thread_id alone must not mean ready. Preserve retained advertised Delve frames, selected frame, optional best-effort locals, timeout with no adapter requests, and once-only wait settlement. Controlled requests must cover continue/re-stop with reused frame IDs, selected-session replacement during each status request, and unrelated-session stop/exit events. Existing MCP suite plus real Delve pause/select-frame roundtrip must pass. Characterize session_status's stale outcome before choosing retry versus structured error; do not silently introduce unbounded retries.

**Effort/risk / leave-alone assessment.** 2–3 days, medium: event order matters more than line count. Current fixes address the observed readiness/frame failures; this is future locality work, not evidence those fixes failed.

title: Localize session-tab serialization ownership and remove obsolete host capability
description:
Backlog recommendation only. User explicitly requested no implementation during stabilization.

Source: independent Sol priority review of eef1446 plus parent fixes; source drift to5df148d recorded. Parent re-read the final wait readiness guard; these remain design recommendations, not reproduced release blockers. Statechart evidence: docs/audits/statechart/2026-11-07/README.md.

**Description / confirmed evidence.** Live tab ownership and marker events live in `host/tab.lua:59–129`; marker field names, file rewriting and number-to-handle consumption live in `vim-sessions.lua:12–43,124–141`. The post-write compatibility branch requires both modules to know when a serialized index becomes authoritative. Current host interface still describes `owns_tabpage` as restore policy (`host/init.lua:21–25`), with implementations at `host/tab.lua:505`, `host/split.lua:145`, `host/remote.lua:668`. Repository-wide search finds **no reads** of that field: current restore uses saved provenance and all-debugger-buffer fallback (`vim-sessions.lua:71–98,163–174`), independent of selected host. This field is confirmed internally unused, not proof of no downstream consumer.

**Proposed seam / deletion.** Put claim/release of the live tab handle plus session-write marker update/consume policy behind one small internal ownership module; the tab adapter supplies its handle, session restoration consumes the saved claim once. Keep filesystem repair only in the compatibility implementation. Delete host-side knowledge of serialized global syntax/index freshness and remove the unused owns_tabpage contract/assignments after checking supported extension compatibility. Do not serialize process-local handles or assume current host config establishes saved ownership.

**Dependencies / sequence.** Independent. First the cheap unused-contract cleanup (or deprecate if public consumers exist); only later move ownership bookkeeping unchanged. Preserve the repaired session-write seam and old-Neovim behavior before considering further reduction. Full extraction is optional if it merely moves the same two-way coordination.

**Acceptance / validation.** Reorder without TabEnter, save/restore across host config changes, globals omitted, mixed source/debugger user tabs, all-debugger stale tabs, last-tab preservation and manual tabclose must keep existing semantics. Test both SessionWritePre and SessionWritePost fallback, patch only an existing serialized global before SessionLoadPost, and consume marker exactly once. Reuse session ownership/restore regressions; never run historical defect-asserting replays against the fixed checkout as passing tests.

**Effort/risk / leave-alone assessment.** 1–2 days, medium/high due to destructive cleanup semantics. Current fix is sufficient; prefer small contract deletion and defer the broader extraction absent repeated ownership changes.

title: No goto / jump-to-line
description: An agent cannot move the instruction pointer. DAP's gotoTargets plus goto requests let a debugger skip or re-run a region without restarting, which is useful for exploring a branch that was not taken. control covers stepping and run_to_line but not this.
design: Two requests: gotoTargets for the file/line, then goto with the chosen target id and the stopped thread. Rarely supported outside a few adapters, so the capability guard matters more than the happy path.
acceptance_criteria: A goto tool resolves gotoTargets for a file and line and jumps there, behind capabilities.supportsGotoTargetsRequest, with a clear message when the adapter lacks it.

title: Breakpoint kinds beyond file:line
description: set_breakpoint takes a file and a line only. DAP also defines function breakpoints (setFunctionBreakpoints), which let an agent break on a symbol without knowing where it lives, and data breakpoints or watchpoints (setDataBreakpoints), which break when a variable changes. Neither is reachable. Function breakpoints are the more useful of the two for an agent, since finding a line number is exactly the step it tends to get wrong.
design: Both are whole-list-replacement requests in DAP, like setBreakpoints: keep the desired set in Lua and resend it on change. nvim-dap has its own breakpoint bookkeeping for line breakpoints; check whether it tracks function breakpoints too before adding a parallel store.
acceptance_criteria: Function breakpoints can be set and listed when the adapter advertises supportsFunctionBreakpoints; data breakpoints likewise behind supportsDataBreakpoints. Unsupported kinds fail with a clear capability message rather than a protocol error.

title: Move the ui_* tools out of the DAP MCP
description: ui_open, ui_close, ui_undock, ui_dock and ui_host drive dap-view's window layout in the human's Neovim. They are editor-surface control, not debug-adapter operations, and they sit awkwardly inside a DAP-shaped tool surface: they already have to degrade to a ui_unavailable error whenever dap-view is absent. They belong in a general-purpose Neovim MCP alongside other editor control, with the DAP server keeping only what speaks to a debug adapter.
design: Deliberately deferred: the shape of the general-purpose Neovim MCP is unknown, and this is a move rather than a fix. When it happens, decide first whether the two surfaces are two servers or one server with namespaced tool groups; the registry in lua/dap-mcp/registry.lua and the Go sidecar are both generic enough to host a second group. tools/ui.lua is self-contained and already guards on ui.integrate_dap_view, so the move itself is small.
acceptance_criteria: The DAP MCP registers only debug-adapter tools. Editor control is reachable from a separate general-purpose Neovim MCP surface, with the registry and sidecar shared rather than duplicated. Existing agent workflows that open or undock the view keep working through the new home.
